items.title: Model deterministic refinance and consolidation scenarios in the debt engine
items.outcome: As a user, I can model a refinance or a consolidation of my existing debts against a hypothetical rate and term and see the deterministic effect on my payoff schedule, without the application ever naming or recommending a lender or a product to me.
items.context: The debt engine already computes amortisation, payoff projection and strategy comparison; this ticket adds what-if scenario modelling on top of that machinery. The regulatory line is absolute: this is a calculator that compares a hypothetical schedule against the real one, never a recommendation engine, so no scenario response may name or rank a lender or a financial product.
scope: Refinance scenario computing a hypothetical schedule from a user-entered rate and term against the current payoff projection
Consolidation scenario combining a chosen set of existing debts into one hypothetical schedule
Explicit statement of every assumption the scenario used, carried in the response rather than left implicit
Side-by-side comparison against the existing payoff projection from the published debt contract
Hard prohibition, enforced in code, on any lender name, product name or ranked recommendation appearing in a response
Disclaimer version identifier carried on every scenario response
acceptance_criteria: A refinance or consolidation scenario is deterministic and reproducible for the same inputs
No response names a lender, a specific financial product or ranks options against each other, proven by a copy scan over every generated field
A scenario is presented as a hypothetical comparison and never applied to the user's real schedule without an explicit separate action
The comparison against the existing payoff projection agrees with the independent model across the case matrix
Every scenario response carries the disclaimer version identifier the client must render
An infeasible consolidation, such as one that increases the effective rate with no other benefit, returns an explicit result rather than a misleadingly favourable one
contracts_schema: Extends the published debt contract with refinance and consolidation scenario request and response shapes
security_privacy: Scenario inputs and outputs are scoped to the requesting user only
No scenario output is sent to any third party or model; the computation is entirely deterministic and server-local
observability: Publishes scenario computation counts and latency without amounts
tests: Copy scan for lender or product names across every generated field
Independent model agreement test against the existing payoff projection
rollout_rollback: Behind a flag; scenarios ship after the copy scan and independent model comparison are green
Rollback hides scenario modelling while the real payoff schedule and projections remain unaffected
non_goals: Any lender or product recommendation, permanently
Any integration with a lender to originate or apply a refinance, permanently
Client presentation, which the android and web debt surfaces own
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns the scenario computation module. Clients render the comparison and assumptions rather than recomputing them.
definition_of_done: Merged only after a current-head core-reviewer attestation from a separate qualified reviewer-agent session
Every acceptance criterion demonstrated by a named automated test or attached evidence
Tests listed in this ticket run in CI and are required by branch protection
Observability, rollout and rollback notes recorded on the ticket before merge
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges
Independent second-reviewer approval obtained under T-GOV-03; where no second reviewer exists yet, an external independent review is a hard blocker and this ticket cannot merge
